name: mailslurp
description: A Pulumi provider that creates and manages MailSlurp email infrastructure.

nodejs.packageDescription: A Pulumi provider that creates and manages MailSlurp email infrastructure.

apiKey.description:
The MailSlurp API key. The provider reads `MAILSLURP_API_KEY` when you
do not set this property. The key is a secret, and Pulumi encrypts it
in the state.

endpoint.description:
The base URL of the MailSlurp API. The default is
`https://api.mailslurp.com`. Set this property only when you test
against a different endpoint.

alternativeRecordEntries.description: The values to use when your DNS provider rejects the main entries.

label.description: The role of the record, for example `VERIFICATION` or `DKIM`.

name.description: The full DNS name of the record.

recordEntries.description: The values of the record. Add one entry for each value.

recordType.description: The DNS record type, for example `TXT`, `MX`, or `CNAME`.

required.description: MailSlurp reports whether the domain needs this record.

ttl.description: The time to live of the record, in seconds.

enum.name: HttpInbox
enum.description: The domain serves inboxes that store email with HTTP endpoints.

enum.name: SmtpDomain
enum.description: The domain serves inboxes that receive email on a real SMTP mail server.

name.description: The name of the variable, without the moustache markers.

variableType.description: The type of the variable. The API reports one value, `STRING`.

enum.name: Recipients
enum.description: MailSlurp compares the addresses that the email went to.

enum.name: Sender
enum.description: MailSlurp compares the address that sent the email.

enum.name: Subject
enum.description: MailSlurp compares the subject of the email.

enum.name: Attachments
enum.description: MailSlurp compares the attachments of the email.

enum.name: AttachmentFilename
enum.description: MailSlurp compares the file name of each attachment.

enum.name: AttachmentText
enum.description: MailSlurp compares the text inside each attachment.

enum.name: And
enum.description: MailSlurp forwards the email when every rule of the group matches.

enum.name: Or
enum.description: MailSlurp forwards the email when one rule of the group matches.

enum.name: Wildcard
enum.description: MailSlurp reads the match value as a pattern. A star matches every character.

enum.name: Match
enum.description: MailSlurp compares the part with the whole match value. The API does not state how this mode differs from `EQUAL`.

enum.name: Contain
enum.description: MailSlurp forwards the email when the part holds the match value inside it.

enum.name: Equal
enum.description: MailSlurp forwards the email when the part and the match value are the same.

groups.description:
The groups that this group holds. Put a group inside a group to build a
deeper tree.

matches.description: The rules that MailSlurp applies to the email.

operator.description:
The way that MailSlurp joins the rules of this group. Use `AND` when
every rule must match. Use `OR` when one rule is enough.

field.description: The part of the email that MailSlurp compares against the `value` property.

should.description: The way that MailSlurp compares the `value` property.

value.description: The value or the pattern that MailSlurp compares.

enum.name: HttpInbox
enum.description: The inbox stores email with HTTP endpoints. Use this type for tests and webhooks.

enum.name: SmtpInbox
enum.description: The inbox receives email on a real SMTP mail server. Use this type for external senders.

enum.name: Block
enum.description: MailSlurp stops the email when the target matches.

enum.name: Allow
enum.description: MailSlurp permits the email when the target matches, and this action wins over a block.

enum.name: FilterRemove
enum.description: MailSlurp removes the matched address from the email, and the rest of the email continues.

enum.name: BounceSoft
enum.description: MailSlurp answers the sender with a soft bounce, which states a temporary failure.

enum.name: BounceHard
enum.description: MailSlurp answers the sender with a hard bounce, which states a permanent failure.

enum.name: ReceivingEmails
enum.description: MailSlurp applies the ruleset to every email that the inbox receives.

enum.name: SendingEmails
enum.description: MailSlurp applies the ruleset to every email that the inbox sends.

enum.name: ReceivingSms
enum.description: MailSlurp applies the ruleset to every SMS message that a phone number receives.

enum.name: SendingSms
enum.description: MailSlurp applies the ruleset to every SMS message that a phone number sends.

enum.name: EmailReceived
enum.description: MailSlurp sends the event when an inbox receives an email payload.

enum.name: NewAiTransformResult
enum.description: MailSlurp sends the event when an AI transformer produces a new extraction result.

enum.name: NewEmail
enum.description: MailSlurp sends the event when an inbox receives a new email.

enum.name: NewContact
enum.description: MailSlurp sends the event when it creates a contact from inbound email activity.

enum.name: NewAttachment
enum.description: MailSlurp sends the event when it detects an attachment on a received email.

enum.name: EmailOpened
enum.description: MailSlurp sends the event when it tracks an email open.

enum.name: EmailRead
enum.description: MailSlurp sends the event when a recipient reads an email.

enum.name: DeliveryStatus
enum.description: MailSlurp sends the event when the delivery status of a sent email changes.

enum.name: Bounce
enum.description: MailSlurp sends the event when an email bounces at the account level.

enum.name: BounceRecipient
enum.description: MailSlurp sends the event when an email address bounces.

enum.name: NewSms
enum.description: MailSlurp sends the event when a phone number receives an SMS message.

enum.name: NewGuestUser
enum.description: MailSlurp sends the event for a guest user.

do not set this property. The key is a secret, and Pulumi encrypts it
in the state.

`https://api.mailslurp.com`. Set this property only when you test

apiKey.description:

in the state.

endpoint.description:

`https://api.mailslurp.com`. Set this property only when you test

createdAt.description: The time when MailSlurp created the template.

name.description: The display name of the template.

variables.description:
The variables that MailSlurp reads from the content. MailSlurp parses this
list on the server, so you cannot set it.

content.description:
The body of the template. Write a variable as `{{firstName}}`, and
MailSlurp reports each variable that it reads in the `variables` property.
You can update this property in place.

name.description: The display name of the template. You can update this property in place.

domain.description: The domain part of the inbox email address.

functionsAs.description: The special function of the inbox, for example an alias or a catch-all.

localPart.description: The local part of the inbox email address.

name.description: The display name of the inbox.

prefix.description: The prefix for the local part of the assigned email address. The API does not echo this property.

readOnly.description: MailSlurp reports whether the inbox is read-only.

useDomainPool.description: The shared MailSlurp domain pool value of the inbox. The API does not echo this property.

useShortAddress.description: The short address value of the inbox. The API does not echo this property.

virtualInbox.description: MailSlurp reports whether the inbox is virtual. A virtual inbox never sends email to real recipients.

description.description:
A free-text description of the inbox. You can update this property in
place. The API cannot clear this property after you set it.

domainId.description:
The identifier of a verified custom domain that provides the inbox
address. **Warning:** If you change this property, Pulumi replaces the inbox. The new inbox counts against the 30-day creation quota, and MailSlurp bills it.

domainName.description:
The custom domain that provides the inbox address. The domain must be
verified in your MailSlurp account. **Warning:** If you change this property, Pulumi replaces the inbox. The new inbox counts against the 30-day creation quota, and MailSlurp bills it.

emailAddress.description:
The full email address of the inbox. When you do not set this
property, MailSlurp assigns an address. **Warning:** If you change this property, Pulumi replaces the inbox. The new inbox counts against the 30-day creation quota, and MailSlurp bills it.

expiresAt.description:
The time when MailSlurp expires the inbox, in RFC 3339 format. You can
update this property in place. The API cannot clear this property after
you set it.

expiresIn.description:
The lifetime of the inbox in milliseconds. The API does not echo this
property, so Pulumi keeps it in the state and does not diff it against
the API. **Warning:** If you change this property, Pulumi replaces the inbox. The new inbox counts against the 30-day creation quota, and MailSlurp bills it.

favourite.description:
If you set this property, MailSlurp marks the inbox as a favourite in
the dashboard. You can update this property in place.

inboxType.description:
The inbox type: `HTTP_INBOX` or `SMTP_INBOX`. A refresh keeps the
prior value when the API does not report a type. **Warning:** If you change this property, Pulumi replaces the inbox. The new inbox counts against the 30-day creation quota, and MailSlurp bills it.

name.description:
The display name of the inbox. You can update this property in place.
The API cannot clear this property after you set it.

prefix.description:
A prefix for the local part of the assigned email address. The API
does not echo this property, so Pulumi keeps it in the state and does
not diff it against the API. **Warning:** If you change this property, Pulumi replaces the inbox. The new inbox counts against the 30-day creation quota, and MailSlurp bills it.

tags.description:
The tags on the inbox. Use tags to group and find inboxes. You can
update this property in place. Set an empty list to clear the tags.

useDomainPool.description:
If you set this property, MailSlurp assigns the address from the shared
domain pool. The API does not echo this property, so Pulumi keeps it in
the state and does not diff it against the API. **Warning:** If you change this property, Pulumi replaces the inbox. The new inbox counts against the 30-day creation quota, and MailSlurp bills it.

useShortAddress.description:
If you set this property, MailSlurp assigns a short email address to the
inbox. The API does not echo this property, so Pulumi keeps it in the
state and does not diff it against the API. **Warning:** If you change this property, Pulumi replaces the inbox. The new inbox counts against the 30-day creation quota, and MailSlurp bills it.

virtualInbox.description:
If you set this property, MailSlurp creates a virtual inbox. A virtual
inbox receives email but never sends it to real recipients. Use it for
safe tests. **Warning:** If you change this property, Pulumi replaces the inbox. The new inbox counts against the 30-day creation quota, and MailSlurp bills it.

createdAt.description: The time when MailSlurp created the forwarder.

field.description: The part of the email that MailSlurp compares.

forwardToRecipients.description: The addresses that MailSlurp sends the matching email to.

inboxId.description: The inbox that the forwarder reads.

match.description: The value or the pattern that MailSlurp compares.

matchOptions.description: The tree of match rules that MailSlurp applies to each email.

name.description:
The display name of the forwarder. MailSlurp writes it, and the create
call takes no name, so you cannot set it.

should.description: The way that MailSlurp compares the `match` value.

field.description:
The part of the email that MailSlurp compares against the `match` value.
You can update this property in place.

forwardToRecipients.description:
The addresses that MailSlurp sends the matching email to. The API
requires this property on every write. You can update this property in
place.

inboxId.description:
The inbox that the forwarder reads. MailSlurp compares each email that
this inbox receives. **Warning:** If you change this property, Pulumi
replaces the forwarder. The new forwarder carries a new identifier.

match.description:
The value or the pattern that MailSlurp compares. Use `*@example.com` to
match every address of a domain. You can update this property in place.

matchOptions.description:
A tree of match rules that MailSlurp applies to each email. The
`operator` property joins the rules of one group. You can put a group
inside the `groups` property. You can update this property in place.

should.description:
The way that MailSlurp compares the `match` value. Use `WILDCARD` for a
pattern that holds a star. Use `EQUAL` for one exact value. You can
update this property in place.

action.description: The action that MailSlurp takes when the target matches.

createdAt.description: The time when MailSlurp created the ruleset.

handler.description: The handler that MailSlurp runs for the ruleset. The API reports one value, `EXCEPTION`.

inboxId.description: The inbox that the ruleset applies to.

phoneId.description:
The phone number that the ruleset applies to. This resource always names
an inbox, so MailSlurp reports no phone number.

scope.description: The activity that the ruleset applies to.

target.description: The email address or the pattern that MailSlurp matches.

action.description:
The action that MailSlurp takes when the target matches. The `ALLOW`
action wins over the `BLOCK` action. The `FILTER_REMOVE` action removes
the matched address and keeps the rest of the email. **Warning:** If you change this property, Pulumi replaces the ruleset. The new ruleset carries a new identifier.

inboxId.description:
The inbox that the ruleset applies to. MailSlurp matches the email of the
inbox against the target. **Warning:** If you change this property, Pulumi replaces the ruleset. The new ruleset carries a new identifier.

scope.description:
The activity that the ruleset applies to. Use `RECEIVING_EMAILS` for the
email the inbox receives. Use `SENDING_EMAILS` for the email the inbox
sends. **Warning:** If you change this property, Pulumi replaces the ruleset. The new ruleset carries a new identifier.

target.description:
The email address or the pattern that MailSlurp matches. Use
`*@example.com` to match every address of a domain. Use one full address
to match that address alone. **Warning:** If you change this property, Pulumi replaces the ruleset. The new ruleset carries a new identifier.

createdAt.description: The time when MailSlurp created the webhook.

enabled.description:
MailSlurp reports whether the webhook is enabled. The API does not
document this property, and the value can be empty.

eventName.description: The event that triggers the webhook.

healthStatus.description:
The health of the webhook, as MailSlurp computes it. The value is
`HEALTHY` or `UNHEALTHY`. The value changes often, so Pulumi never
compares it.

ignoreInsecureSslCertificates.description: MailSlurp reports whether it accepts an insecure SSL certificate on your server.

inboxId.description:
The inbox that triggers the webhook. An empty value means that every
inbox in the account triggers the webhook.

includeHeaders.description:
The HTTP headers that MailSlurp sends with each webhook request. The API
names this value `requestHeaders` when it reports it.

method.description: The HTTP method that your server must accept. MailSlurp sends `POST`.

name.description: The display name of the webhook.

requestBodyTemplate.description: The template for the JSON body of the webhook request.

url.description: The URL that MailSlurp posts the event payload to.

useStaticIpRange.description: MailSlurp reports whether it calls your server from its static IP range.

eventName.description:
The event that triggers the webhook. If you do not set this property,
MailSlurp sends the `EMAIL_RECEIVED` event.

ignoreInsecureSslCertificates.description:
If you set this property, MailSlurp accepts an insecure SSL certificate
on your server. Use it for a self-signed certificate. The default value
is false.

inboxId.description:
The inbox that triggers the webhook. If you do not set this property,
every inbox in the account triggers the webhook. You can move the webhook
to another inbox in place. You cannot remove this property after you set
it, because the API has no value for the account.

includeHeaders.description:
The HTTP headers that MailSlurp sends with each webhook request. Each key
is a header name, and each value is the header value. The provider marks
the values as secret. MailSlurp reports the values as plain text, so
anyone with the API key can read them.

name.description:
The display name of the webhook. You can update this property in place.
Remove the property to clear the name.

requestBodyTemplate.description:
A template for the JSON body of the webhook request. Use `{{variableName}}`
markers to insert values from the event payload.

tags.description:
The tags on the webhook. MailSlurp accepts the tags and never reports
them, so Pulumi cannot compare this property. A change to the tags alone
plans no update.

url.description:
The URL that MailSlurp posts the event payload to. Your server must
accept the request. You can update this property in place.

useStaticIpRange.description:
If you set this property, MailSlurp calls your server from its static IP
range. The default value is false.

mailslurp:index:getDomain.description:
The function reads one MailSlurp custom domain by its identifier. The
result carries the DNS records that the domain needs, so a stack can
create them with a DNS provider. The function reads the domain and
changes nothing.

checkForErrors.description:
If you set this property, MailSlurp checks the domain for DNS record
problems. The default is `false`.

domainId.description:
The identifier of the domain to read. MailSlurp assigns this value when
it creates the domain.

catchAllInboxId.description:
The identifier of the inbox that receives the email of every unmatched
address.

createdAt.description: The time when MailSlurp created the domain.

dkimTokens.description: The DKIM values of the domain. Add one CNAME record for each value.

domainNameRecords.description:
The DNS records that the domain needs. Loop over this list to create the
records with a DNS provider.

duplicateRecordsMessage.description: The message that names the duplicate DNS records.

hasDuplicateRecords.description: MailSlurp reports whether the domain has a duplicate DNS record.

hasMissingRecords.description: MailSlurp reports whether the domain misses a required DNS record.

isVerified.description: MailSlurp reports whether the domain passed the DNS checks.

missingRecordsMessage.description: The message that names the missing DNS records.

updatedAt.description: The time when MailSlurp last changed the domain.

verificationToken.description:
The value that proves you own the domain. Add it to the DNS records of
the domain.

mailslurp:index:getInbox.description:
The function reads one MailSlurp inbox by its identifier. Use it when a
stack must reference an inbox that Pulumi does not manage. The function
reads the inbox and changes nothing.

inboxId.description:
The identifier of the inbox to read. MailSlurp assigns this value when
it creates the inbox.

accountRegion.description: The region of the account that holds the inbox.

createdAt.description: The time when MailSlurp created the inbox.

description.description: The free-text description of the inbox.

domain.description: The domain part of the inbox email address.

domainId.description: The identifier of the custom domain that provides the inbox address.

emailAddress.description: The full email address of the inbox.

expiresAt.description: The time when MailSlurp expires the inbox, in RFC 3339 format.

favourite.description: MailSlurp reports whether the inbox is a favourite in the dashboard.

functionsAs.description: The special function of the inbox, for example an alias or a catch-all.

localPart.description: The local part of the inbox email address.

name.description: The display name of the inbox.

readOnly.description: MailSlurp reports whether the inbox is read-only.

virtualInbox.description: MailSlurp reports whether the inbox is virtual. A virtual inbox never sends email to real recipients.
